correctness.rationale: For a candidate losing word with both letters, each ab prefix deletion leaves a b-to-a word, and each ba suffix deletion leaves an a-to-b word; pure words have no moves. A complementary word beginning in b or ending in b can be moved to a pure b-word, including the empty word. For a complementary word with both ends a, cutting at the first singleton b-run leaves a candidate losing prefix. This proves the P/N classification by length induction. Run minima consume 3j+1 letters; distributing slack among 2j+1 runs gives the binomial sum and the geometric series yields the rational function. The cubic in lambda has discriminant -23, so its root lambda in (1,2) dominates the two conjugate roots of modulus lambda^(-1/2); the simple-pole coefficient equals the stated C. Deletion lowers length by at least two, and even-length prefix cuts of the alternating word realize every smaller Grundy value, including at the empty-word boundary. A fresh length-0-through-17 exhaustive mex and enumeration replay passed, but the all-length claims rest on these proofs.
residual_risks: The replay is finite and does not check the original uploaded programs or constitute a formal proof.
